intro.description: Step-by-step guide for creating a course.json file that works in both the RCP desktop and web browser hosts. See Schema_Course_JSON_CLAUDE_V1.json for the full schema and Spec_Course_Security_CLAUDE_V1_1.md for security constraints.

item.title: 1. Create the course file
item.description: Create a new file named courses/my_course.json. Start with the required top-level fields.

subitem.label: Set schemaVersion to '1.0'.
Set course to your course title (max 200 chars).
Set locale to 'en' (or 'fr' for French command names).
Add a tree array with at least one chapter.

item.title: 2. Structure chapters and steps
item.description: Each chapter has a title and children (array of steps). Steps can nest up to 4 levels deep (5 total with the chapter). Keep courses under 50 chapters and 500 total actions.

subitem.label: Each chapter needs title (required) and children (required, at least one step).
Each step needs title (required). actions and check are optional.
A step with no actions is informational (description only).

item.title: 3. Write actions (directives)
item.description: Actions are the commands GeoGebra executes when the student clicks Run Step. Each action has a directive type and a value.

subitem.label: CMD: evalCommand — e.g. 'A = (1, 2)' or 'c = Circle(O, 1)'.
CAS: evalCommandCAS — e.g. 'Simplify(cos(x)^2 + sin(x)^2)'.
VAL: read a value — e.g. 'x(A)' to display the x-coordinate of A.
OPEN: load a .ggb file — path must be relative, under the course directory, ending in .ggb.
SAVE / PNG: save construction or export screenshot (desktop only).

item.title: 4. Add validation checks
item.description: Checks give formative feedback when the student clicks the Check button. They are NOT grades — grades come from WIMS server-side.

subitem.label: object_exists: check if a named object exists — e.g. variable: 'O'.
value_equals: compare a numeric value — e.g. variable: 'y(A)', expected: 2.0, tolerance: 0.001.
value_range: check a range — e.g. expected: {min: 0.706, max: 0.708}.
cas_equals: compare CAS output — e.g. variable: 'Simplify(sin(x)^2+cos(x)^2)', expected: '1'.
Add feedback.pass and feedback.fail messages for student guidance.

item.title: 5. Security constraints
item.description: The course executor enforces an allowlist. Blocked commands will be rejected at runtime. See the security spec for the full list.

subitem.label: TABLE_SCRIPTING commands are blocked: Execute, RunClickScript, RunUpdateScript, ExportImage, etc.
Individual blocks: Delete, Rename, Pan, ZoomIn/Out, CenterView, SetPerspective.
Safe styling allowed: SetColor, SetPointStyle, SetLineThickness, SetCaption, ShowLabel, SetFixed, Slider, Checkbox.
OPEN paths: no .., no absolute paths, no URLs, .ggb extension only.
Sequence limit: max 10,000 iterations.

item.title: 6. Target 2D vs 3D
item.description: On the RCP desktop, there are separate 2D and 3D GeoGebra instances. Specify which one each action targets.

subitem.label: Default target is '2d' (omit the field for 2D commands).
Set target: '3d' for 3D commands like Point(1,2,3) or Plane(A,B,C).
On the web, both targets go to the same applet (3D view must be open).

item.title: 7. Validate and test
item.description: Before distributing, validate your course file against the JSON schema.

subitem.label: VS Code task 'Schema: Validate course file' runs jsonschema validation.
Launch with: launch.ps1 -Course courses/my_course.json (desktop).
Or open course-host.html?course=courses/my_course.json (web).
Check that all steps execute and all checks pass/fail as expected.

item.title: 8. Include .ggb files
item.description: If your course loads pre-built constructions, place .ggb files in the same directory as course.json.

subitem.label: Use OPEN directive with a relative path: 'constructions/setup.ggb'.
The .ggb file is scanned for embedded scripts. Files with geogebra_javascript.js, script elements, or ggbscript blocks are rejected.
Set trustedGgb: true only if you vouch for the embedded scripts.
